# Combat scoring training file — merged and normalized corpus.
#
# @domain_priority: cross:element, items:combat_archetypes, items:universal_tags, items:item_only_tags, items:weapon_tags, items:armor_tags, items:helmet_tags, items:boots_tags, items:gloves_tags, items:trouser_tags, items:bracer_tags, items:cape_tags, items:amulet_tags, items:ring_tags, items:rune_tags, items:device_tags, items:tool_tags, items:utility_tags, items:socketable_tags, items:craft_material_tags, items:craft_recipe_tags, items:key_tags, common:common_tags, terrain:terrain_only_tags, weather:weather_only_tags, zone:zone_tags, realm:realm_tags, npcs:personality, harvestables:harvest_process, growables:growth_process, enemies:combat, pets:pet_tags, npcs, harvestables, growables, pets, items:craft_material, items:weapon, items:armor, items:tool, items:utility, items:rune
#
# Two kinds of lines:
#
#   def <id> = <token> <token> ...
#       Defines a named token bag. The id can then be referenced from
#       scenario lines as a shortcut. Tokens are tags, element names,
#       material names, or other descriptors the model should see.
#
#   <attacker_tokens> | <defender_tokens> | <score>
#       One training scenario. Tokens are space-separated. A token may
#       be a `def` id (expands to its bag) or a raw tag. Score is a
#       float in [0.0, 1.0]: 1 = guaranteed perfect hit, 0 = miss.
#
# This file is the cleaned English merge of the old combat.txt and combat2.txt.
#
# SCORING RULE (written down 2026-11-11 after an audit found the file was
# applying three different logics side by side).  Judge every new line by it:
#
#   1. MATERIAL sets the base.  Heavy/sharp against light/soft scores high;
#      blunt against plate scores low; a non-weapon against armour is near 0.
#   2. ELEMENT modifies, but only where the element is the DEFINING trait of
#      both sides (a lightning weapon against a storm robe).  Opposing element
#      +0.10, same element -0.15.  Incidental overlap does not count: `aether`
#      sits in many bags, and a sharp blade against brittle glass armour stays
#      high because rule 1 decides it.
#   3. TARGET SIZE modifies.  A small target (ring, glove, bracer) -0.25;
#      armour, cloaks and robes unchanged.
#
# ONLY WEAPONS ATTACK.  The attacker column holds weapons; armour, jewellery,
# boots, capes, vials and recipes belong on the defender side.  85 lines of the
# old coverage blocks paired a healing vial or a craft recipe AGAINST armour --
# they taught the model nonsense and were removed 2026-11-11.
#
# A line must not restate tokens that its own `def` bag already contains: the
# score difference it claims is then unexplainable (53 lines did this; the
# three that contradicted each other outright were resolved).
#
# Two `def` spellings exist — `def id = tokens` and, in the later coverage
# blocks, `def id [name=…,type=…] = tokens`.  A parser must handle both; one
# that splits on the first `=` reads 25 of the 82 bags as garbage.
